findings.reason: the queue orders only declared waits, so §2 could launch before §8 lands in the same file and §4 before §3, producing exactly the cross-worktree collision the wait exists to prevent.
findings.text: §2 declares "it runs after `a-promotion-reads-the-evidence-it-is-given` §8, which also writes `promotion_evidence.py`", and §4 declares "it runs after §3" (l. 57), yet the plan carries no `plan-depends-on` meta and no `plan-section-depends-on` meta (its only relationship is `plan-informs`, l. 22)

findings.reason: a node dispatched on the stated write path cannot make the change, and §2's done-when even names the wrong module for its base arm ("test files importing `reckon.crew.promotion_evidence`"), so the node would either stop on a scope blocker or edit a module the reader never runs.
findings.text: §1 cites the control-log contract to `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py` near lines 1021–1092 and §2 (l. 46–47) names that same file as the control-evidence reader and as a write path, but that module imports no control logic and the reader that raises the cited refusal is `_require_declared_negative_control` in `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py` (near lines 2029–2210)

findings.reason: the floor yields 60 m for the very 3 h H200 job §1 says needs 240 m, so §5's title ("never budgets below the compute a brief names") is not produced by its mechanism and the fire the plan was written to put out still burns one fence-width lower.
findings.text: §3 and §4 record a 60 m resolved fence while §1 (l. 37) records 240 m, 120 m and 90 m work refused for exceeding it, yet §5 (l. 61) has the picker floor a heavy gate's budget at "the resolved fence"

findings.reason: the mechanism would be written where no budget is assigned and no caller reaches it, so the 8 m default survives and the node's gate passes on a change that never runs on the production path.
findings.text: the budget §5 says the picker assigns is not assigned in `reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py`; that module only reads a node's declared budget to classify its size (`_size_of`, l. 173/388), while the assignment is `node.time_budget = node.time_budget or resolved_time_budget(config, backend)` in `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:800` resolving through `reckon/crew/routing.py:505`

findings.reason: the plan cites no run, plan or review record reproducing the §6 halt, and a node that does not first reproduce against the existing judge will build a second coverage route beside `review_need` and `_acted_finding_units`; unlike §2, §5 and §7, §6 names no reproduce-first step for the defect it claims.
findings.text: §6 asserts "an edit that does exactly what a stored finding asked still uncovers the section and owes a new review" and its done-when asserts that pre-state, but `review_coverage` already covers such edits: `_acted_finding_units` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2707`) covers a unit whose findings were answered `acted` when the edit stays under the word-share threshold, and the pending remainder is judged by `review_need.judge` (called at l. 1302) which covers a change judged not to need a review

response_events.reason: the shared files are serialised by write-path claims: dispatch refuses a node whose write paths a live run holds, naming the owner, so the order needs no plan wait

wiring-1.reason: the shared files are serialised by write-path claims: dispatch refuses a node whose write paths a live run holds, naming the owner, so the order needs no plan wait

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the control-evidence reader §1 and §2 cite is not in `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py`; that file contains no control reader at all (`grep -cni negative reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py` = 0) and its cited lines 1021–1092 are the gate-log readers `_log_shows_the_command_ran` and `_require_gate_log_agrees`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — every section names a specific mutation whose removal makes a named case refuse (§2 re-requiring `EXIT=`, §3 ignoring the recorded reason, §4 ignoring the option, §5 removing the floor, §6 ignoring the acceptance record, §7 passing the stored flag again), so each gate can show its guard fires.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — no gate log or evidence artifact is placed on a scratchpad or node-local path; every section's measure is an in-repository test file and the mutation log stays on the worker's manifest-recorded path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the proposed symbols and test filenames are mechanism-named (`test_a_negative_control_is_read_from_the_runner.py`, `--over-fence`, `--accept-edits`); the only identifiers in the prose are run ids and plan slugs, which are evidence, not code.
rubric_items.reasoning: three findings — §2's mechanism names a module that does not hold the reader, §5's floor cannot satisfy §5's own title and §1's own evidence, and §6's premise is contradicted by an existing mechanism the plan does not cite.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one deliverable; §2's added prompt sentence (l. 46) is a recurrence guard for the same contract rather than an independent deliverable, and one test file asserts both.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §2 states it runs after `a-promotion-reads-the-evidence-it-is-given` §8 and §4 states it runs after §3, but the plan declares neither `plan-depends-on` nor `plan-section-depends-on`.
